info.title: Libre VMM REST API
info.description:
A libre alternative to VMware Workstation, with a real REST API that VMware Workstation does not provide.

## Authentication

All endpoints except `GET /api/v1/health` and the docs themselves require an `X-API-Key` header. The key is printed once on stderr when the server starts (or set via `--api-key`).

```
curl -H 'X-API-Key: <key>' http://127.0.0.1:8420/api/v1/vms
```

## Rate limiting

After 10 failed auth attempts within 60 s the server locks out **all** requests for 5 minutes. This is a global limiter (per-IP is trivially bypassed via proxies).

## Errors

All 4xx/5xx responses share the [`ApiErrorResponse`] envelope. Internal error details (libvirt messages, file paths) are scrubbed server-side (CWE-209).

get.description: Returns server status without contacting libvirt. Does NOT require an API key — safe for load balancers and uptime checks. `libvirt_connected` is always returned as `false`; use `/api/v1/system/info` for the real value.
Returns the hypervisor product/version, KVM availability, and connection family. The full libvirt connection URI is deliberately omitted (CWE-200).
Returns every VM defined in the hypervisor, including running, paused, and shut-off VMs. No pagination — the list is typically small (single-user workstation use case).

post.description: Defines a new VM from a built-in template. The VM is created in the `shut off` state — call `POST /api/v1/vms/{name}/start` to boot it. All numeric fields are clamped to safe ranges; oversized strings and path-traversal in `iso_path` are rejected.

400.description: Invalid request (bad name, out-of-range numbers, etc.)

get.summary: Get a single VM by name
get.description: Returns details of one VM. The `name` path parameter is validated server-side (1-64 chars, alphanumerics + `-_.`) before being passed to libvirt.

delete.description: Removes the VM definition AND the backing disk images. This is irreversible. If the VM is running it will be force-stopped first.

post.description: Creates a copy of an existing VM. `full` clones produce an independent disk image. `linked` clones use copy-on-write on top of the source disk, which is fast but ties the clone to the source's lifecycle.

post.summary: Start a noVNC browser console for a running VM
post.description: Spawns a noVNC proxy that bridges the VM's VNC server to a browser-friendly WebSocket. The returned URL can be opened in any browser. The VM must be running. The proxy continues to run until the API server exits.

400.description: VM not running or invalid ports

post.description: Suspends VM execution while keeping its memory resident. Resume with `/resume`.
Sends an ACPI reboot signal to the guest OS. The guest may ignore it.
Resumes execution of a VM that was paused via `/pause`.
Sends an ACPI shutdown signal to the guest OS. The guest may ignore it. For an unconditional power-off use `/stop` instead.

get.description: Returns every snapshot defined for the given VM, oldest first. An empty list is returned (not 404) when the VM has no snapshots.

post.description: Captures the current VM state (and memory, if running) as a named snapshot. The snapshot name must be 1-128 chars (alphanumerics + ` -_.()`) and must not start with `-`. The description must not contain `<`, `>`, or `&` (XML injection defense, CWE-91).

delete.description: Removes a snapshot from the VM. The VM itself is not affected. Irreversible.

post.description: Rolls the VM back to the state captured by the snapshot. Any state written since the snapshot is discarded.
Boots a previously-created VM. Returns 409 if the VM is already running.
Immediately powers off the VM (equivalent to pulling the plug). Risks data loss in the guest. Prefer `/shutdown` for clean shutdowns.

ApiErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope returned for all 4xx and 5xx responses.

code.description: HTTP status code, duplicated in the body for client convenience.

error.description: Human-readable error description. Internal details are stripped server-side.

clone_type.description: Clone type: `full` (independent copy) or `linked` (copy-on-write, shares base disk). Defaults to `full`.

new_name.description: Name for the cloned VM (same validation rules as VM creation).

listen_port.description: Non-privileged listen port for the noVNC proxy (>= 1024). Defaults to 6080.

vnc_port.description: VNC port of the running VM. Defaults to 5900.

port.description: TCP port the noVNC proxy is listening on.

url.description: Browser URL that serves the noVNC client (open in any browser).

description.description: Optional description (max 1024 chars). Must not contain `<`, `>`, or `&`.

name.description: Snapshot name (1-128 chars, alphanumerics + ` -_.()`). Must not start with `-`.

CreateVmRequest.description:
SECURITY: `deny_unknown_fields` rejects payloads with unexpected keys (CWE-20).
This prevents mass-assignment style attacks and limits deserialization surface.

disk_size_gib.description: Primary disk size in GiB (1 - 16384). Defaults to 25.

iso_path.description: Optional path to a boot ISO on the host. Must not contain `..`.

name.description: VM name (1-64 chars, alphanumerics + `-_.`). Must be unique.

template.description: Template ID or label substring. Defaults to `arch-linux`.

libvirt_connected.description:
Libvirt connection status. Always `false` over this endpoint —
it is intentionally redacted from the unauthenticated health probe.
Use `GET /api/v1/system/info` (authenticated) for the real value.

status.description: Always `"ok"` if the server is reachable.

message.description: Human-readable status message describing the action result.

creation_time.description: ISO-8601-ish timestamp string of when the snapshot was taken.

description.description: Free-form description supplied at creation time.

state.description: VM state captured by the snapshot (`running`, `shutoff`, etc.).

SystemInfoResponse.description:
SECURITY: connection_uri deliberately excluded — it can contain socket paths
and host information that aids reconnaissance (CWE-200).

kvm_available.description: Whether KVM acceleration is available on the host.

count.description: Number of VMs in `vms`. Mirrors `vms.len()` for client convenience.

vms.description: All VMs known to the hypervisor (regardless of state).

cpu_time_ns.description: Cumulative CPU time consumed by the VM in nanoseconds.
